- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (days 1–5); apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5 days.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.2→1.0 or vice versa), model reacts too quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use sentiment-weighted average.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price near 70–72, model tends to hold or overreact; cap forecast at 72.5–73.5 unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- Sentiment decay (e.g., 0.8→0.2) triggers model overcorrection; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days to avoid “panic sell” overreaction.
